steps.what: Build packets of related information for the meeting.
Prepare meeting agendas from the submitted items.

loop.input: the submitted items and the agenda order rule
loop.check: every item id on the agenda is in the packet
loop.stop: stop when an item has no title
loop.why_not_simpler: item titles are free text and the order rule is local

steps.what: Approve the agenda before it is sent.

tasks.design: Submitted items become a packet in {DOCS}, and a meeting agenda is prepared in the order the council rule states. The registry clerk approves the agenda before it is sent to the chair and members. An item with no title is left off. The draft does not add an item nobody submitted.
tasks.previous_blocker: The packet was collated by hand the night before, and a late paper was missing.
tasks.enabler_now: Items already in the store can be ordered by a written rule. The chair's agenda is still approved by the clerk's check.
tasks.still_hard: A chair adds or pulls an item after the packet is built.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk knows which late paper the chair will insist on, and which closed item must not go in the public pack.

ambition.what: Prepare the packet for a small committee the day its items arrive, not only for the main council meeting.

tasks.altitude: Collating a complete packet takes less of the night. The clerk still approves what is sent, and still withholds a closed item.

reach.task: Assemble a meeting pack from documents already filed.
reach.learn: Assembly is not the chair's decision. This clerk still approves the agenda.

evidence.claim: Items with ids and titles can be ordered into an agenda. An item that was not submitted cannot be invented.
Sending an agenda is an external act of the clerk. Closed items are a legal choice about what the public may see. The clerk makes that choice.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Item id, title, and public or closed flag, produced by the person who submitted the item. No title means the item is left off. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing meeting papers in {DOCS} before a new packet tool.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Who may add an item after the packet closes.
research_questions: What share of items arrive with a title and a flag?
How often does the chair change the order?

already_counted.description: The clerk still approves the agenda before it is sent.

incremental.description: The clerk updates the order rule when the council changes it.

approvals.approved_version: meeting id and the agenda text shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If items arrive without titles, the clerk still builds the agenda by hand and the saving stays near the low end. Titled items and a written order keep the high end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record, edit, and distribute meeting minutes.

steps.what: Record the minutes of the meetings.
Edit the minutes draft from the clerk's notes.

loop.input: the clerk's notes and the minute template
loop.check: every decision line cites a note line
loop.stop: stop when a decision has no note line
loop.why_not_simpler: debate wording is free text, not a fixed form

steps.what: Check the minutes against the clerk's notes.
Distribute signed minutes to officials and staff members.

tasks.design: The registry clerk records the minutes in the room. A draft in {DOCS} is edited from those notes, and the clerk checks every decision line against the notes before anyone sees it. Signed minutes then go to the named officials and staff. No new recording of the meeting is added. A decision with no note line is not written into the draft.
tasks.previous_blocker: Minutes were typed from memory the next day, and a decision that felt likely was sometimes written as if it had passed.
tasks.enabler_now: Notes taken in the room can be turned into a draft. The check against those notes stays with the clerk.
tasks.still_hard: A noisy debate and a decision that was unclear even in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk was in the room and can say that a line in the draft was not what was decided.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still attends and still checks the minutes. Typing a clean draft from clear notes takes less of the next morning.

reach.task: Write up a meeting from notes taken in the room.
reach.learn: The notes are the source. This clerk still checks the decision lines before distribution.

evidence.claim: A draft can follow note lines. It cannot add a decision the notes do not contain.
The job digest says call recording and staff monitoring need works-council consent. This task does not add a recorder. Distribution waits for the clerk's check. Minutes are not a justice sentence.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Meeting id and the clerk's note lines, produced by the clerk in the room. A decision line in the draft must cite a note line. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing minute template in {DOCS} before a new one.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
No audio or video recording is introduced by this task.
unknowns: Whether meetings are already recorded under a works-council agreement.
research_questions: How often is a distributed minute corrected?

already_counted.description: The clerk still records the meeting.
The clerk still checks the minutes.

incremental.description: The clerk updates the minute template when the required headings change.

approvals.approved_version: meeting id and the minutes text shown against the notes
checked minutes id and the recipient list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The clerk still sits in the meeting. Saving is the draft from clear notes, and it shrinks when notes are too thin to cite a decision line.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train clerks and coordinate their day.

steps.what: List procedures a new clerk must learn.
Train other workers on the live counter.
Coordinate their work when the list changes.

tasks.design: A reading list of written procedures can be shown from {DOCS}. Training other workers on the live counter stays with the registry clerk, as does coordinating their work when the day's list changes. The list does not certify anyone and does not score them. No dashboard of clerk performance is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: New clerks learned by standing beside whoever was free, and the same mistake was taught twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Written procedures can be listed. Showing someone the counter cannot be listed away.
tasks.still_hard: A busy counter, a new permit type, and people who learn by doing rather than reading.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees the moment a colleague is about to accept a document they should return, and says so.
tasks.altitude: Nothing important moves. A reading list exists. Training and the day's coordination stay in the room with the clerk.

reach.task: Show a new interviewer how to ask the questions without deciding the case for them.
reach.learn: A list of procedures is not training. This clerk still stands at the counter with the new person.

evidence.claim: A catalogue can list procedures. It cannot train a person on a live counter.
The job digest says emotion recognition is prohibited and staff dashboards need works-council consent. This task adds no score and no recording of clerks.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Procedure id and title, produced by the procedure catalogue. The reading list does not store a result against a named clerk. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Link the existing procedure documents before building a course.
unknowns: Whether a works council already limits monitoring of the counter.
research_questions: How are new clerks trained today?

already_counted.description: The clerk still trains colleagues at the counter.
The clerk still coordinates the day's work.

incremental.description: The clerk adds a procedure title when a new counter task is written down.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Training is the task. The only saving is finding the procedure page, and even that disappears if the catalogue is empty and the clerk still explains everything aloud.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer licensing questions and give advice.

steps.what: Show licensing procedures from the approved card.
Provide advice to the public on licensing policies.
Add a regulation the card does not contain.

tasks.design: An approved card in {DOCS} shows the licensing procedure that matches the question. The registry clerk provides advice on policies and regulations when the card is not enough. A machine answer, if the card is shown on a public page, must say it is a machine and must not invent a rule. The clerk adds a missing regulation only after checking it. The card does not tell a resident that they qualify.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every procedure question was answered from memory, so two clerks gave two versions.
tasks.enabler_now: A maintained card can answer a procedure question. Advice about a person's situation cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Residents describe a plan, not a procedure name, and the policy may have changed last month.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk hears the difference between 'what is the fee' and 'will you give me this licence'.

ambition.what: Give the procedure card the same day to a resident who only asks how to apply, including people who now wait behind advice appointments.

tasks.altitude: Procedure questions leave the advice queue. The clerk still advises on policy, and still decides what may be added to the card.

reach.role: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
reach.task: Answer from the house rules, and fetch a person when the guest's question is not on the card.
reach.learn: A card can state a procedure. Advice that someone will qualify is not on the card.

evidence.claim: A card can show a procedure the office has approved. It cannot advise on a resident's own plan.

The job digest says that from 2 August 2026 a machine chat must say it is a machine, and an answer desk must hand off when the question becomes advice. Qualification is not answered here. No emotion recognition is used.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Procedure id and the approved card text, produced by the clerk's office. The card has no field for a person's qualification. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing intranet page of procedures before a new desk.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Which policies are stable enough to put on a card.
Whether the public page is allowed to answer at all.
research_questions: What share of questions are pure procedure?

already_counted.description: The clerk still gives licensing advice.
The clerk still adds a missing regulation.

incremental.description: The clerk reviews the card when a licensing rule changes.

approvals.approved_version: card id and the new regulation text shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If most questions are advice about a person's plan, the clerk still answers them and the saving stays near the low end. Clear procedure questions keep the high end.

role.altitude: The clerk still sits in the meeting, still trains new clerks, and still gives licensing advice. Agenda assembly and approved cards leave the hour.
reach: Medical secretaries prepare a meeting pack from items already sent, and this desk learns the chair still owns the agenda.
Hotel desk clerks answer from a card, and this desk learns when a licensing question has become advice.
skills_to_grow: Keep a minute tied to the note taken in the room, and do not add a decision that was not made.
Answer a licensing procedure from the card, and bring policy questions to the clerk.
role.ambitious_version: A committee packet is ready the day the items arrive, and training a new clerk on the counter still takes the clerk's time.
